# Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T) {#gdt}

```{r setup-01-04, include=FALSE}
# Include the helpers.R file for pdf output of youtube on pdfs as a clickable link
source("R/helpers.R")
# Include the required packages to make sure the page can be built
source("R/required_packages.R")
```

## Learning Objectives {-}

By the end of this chapter, you will be able to:

- Understand the fundamental principles of GD&T per ASME Y14.5 standards
- Differentiate between dimensional and geometric tolerances
- Apply datums, tolerance zones, and modifier symbols correctly
- Create and interpret feature control frames
- Understand the hierarchy of geometric controls
- Apply GD&T to real-world engineering problems
- Use interactive visualizations to verify tolerance stack-up

::: {.callout-think}
**Before You Read:** Traditional plus-minus tolerancing creates a square
tolerance zone. Why might a circular tolerance zone be more appropriate for
locating a hole? Think about how a bolt fits into a hole.
:::

## Introduction to GD&T

Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T) is a standardized method of specifying and communicating engineering tolerances. Unlike traditional plus-minus dimensioning, GD&T uses a symbolic language that provides a clear, concise description of part geometry and allowable variations.

### Why GD&T Matters

Traditional dimensioning (@fig-traditional-vs-gdt) can lead to:

- Ambiguous interpretations of design intent
- Excessive part cost due to overly tight tolerances
- Functional failures due to under-constrained features
- Increased manufacturing costs and waste

GD&T solves these problems by:

- Clearly communicating design intent
- Maximizing functional tolerance zones
- Reducing manufacturing costs
- Improving part interchangeability

::: {.callout-industry}
**Industry Application:** In aerospace and automotive manufacturing, GD&T is
the normal language of production drawings, and OEMs such as Boeing, Airbus,
Ford and GM write it into their drawing standards and supplier requirements. A single misinterpreted tolerance could result in parts that don't
fit, leading to costly rework or safety issues.
:::
```{r fig-traditional-vs-gdt, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=6, fig.align='center', fig.cap="Hole-location zones compared (enlarged, deviations from true position in mm): coordinate tolerances of ±0.25 mm give a square zone; a Ø0.71 mm position zone passes through the square's corners and accepts 57 % more area."}
## Square zone from +/-0.25 coordinate tolerances against the circle through its corners
tq <- 0.25
rc <- tq * sqrt(2)                                  # 0.354 -> position tolerance Ø0.71
cz <- data.frame(x = rc * cos(seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 200)), y = rc * sin(seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 200)))
pts <- data.frame(x = c(0.25, 0.33, 0.12), y = c(0.25, 0, -0.10),
                  lab = c("A: corner of the square,\n0.354 from true position\naccepted by both",
                          "B: 0.33 from true position\nrejected by \u00b10.25 in X,\naccepted by \u00d80.71",
                          "C: well inside\naccepted by both"))

ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = cz, aes(x, y), fill = "lightblue", alpha = 0.5, color = "blue", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = -tq, xmax = tq, ymin = -tq, ymax = tq), fill = "orange", alpha = 0.35, color = "darkorange3", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "F282", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "F282", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = rc * cos(pi / 4), yend = rc * sin(pi / 4)), color = "blue", linewidth = 0.5,
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.12, "cm"))) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.01, y = 0.30, label = "r = 0.354", color = "blue", hjust = 1, size = 3.2 * diagram_text_scale) +
  geom_point(data = pts, aes(x, y), size = 2.5) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.30, y = 0.37, label = pts$lab[1], hjust = 0, size = 3 * diagram_text_scale) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.37, y = 0.11, label = pts$lab[2], hjust = 0, size = 3 * diagram_text_scale) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.06, y = -0.16, label = pts$lab[3], hjust = 0, size = 3 * diagram_text_scale) +
  annotate("text", x = -0.62, y = -0.40, label = "Square zone \u00b10.25 in X and Y\narea 0.25 mm\u00b2",
           color = "darkorange3", fontface = "bold", hjust = 0, size = 3.2 * diagram_text_scale) +
  annotate("text", x = -0.62, y = 0.38, label = "Position zone \u00d80.71\narea 0.39 mm\u00b2 (+57 %)",
           color = "blue", fontface = "bold", hjust = 0, size = 3.2 * diagram_text_scale) +
  annotate("text", x = -0.015, y = -0.02, label = "true
position", hjust = 1, vjust = 1, size = 2.8 * diagram_text_scale) +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(-0.62, 0.75), ylim = c(-0.47, 0.45)) +
  labs(title = "Traditional \u00b1 Coordinates vs. GD&T Position",
       x = "X deviation from true position (mm)", y = "Y deviation (mm)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))
```

## Fundamental Principles

### The Rule of Interchangeability

GD&T is built on the principle that parts must be interchangeable while satisfying functional requirements. This means:

- All parts produced to specification must fit and function together
- Tolerance zones maximize functional space
- Manufacturing processes can operate at economical levels

### Key Definitions

**Datum**: A theoretically exact geometric reference (plane, line, or point) from which other geometric characteristics are measured.

**Tolerance Zone**: The allowable area or volume within which a feature must lie.

**Feature of Size**: A cylindrical feature (hole, shaft) or a pair of parallel surfaces (slot width) to which a tolerance is applied.

**Maximum Material Condition (MMC)**: The condition where a feature contains the maximum amount of material (smallest hole, largest shaft).

**Least Material Condition (LMC)**: The condition where a feature contains the minimum amount of material (largest hole, smallest shaft).

## The Feature Control Frame

The Feature Control Frame (FCF) is the foundation of GD&T notation. It's a rectangular box divided into compartments that specify the geometric characteristic and its requirements.
```{r fcf-diagram, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=3.6, fig.align='center', fig.cap="Feature Control Frame Structure: a position tolerance of Ø0.5 at MMC referenced to datums A, B and C. Each compartment is numbered as in the table below."}
## Feature control frame drawn from coordinates; the position symbol and the circled M are built as geometry
circ <- function(cx, cy, r, n = 100) { a <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = n); data.frame(x = cx + r * cos(a), y = cy + r * sin(a)) }
xb <- c(0, 1.2, 4.6, 5.8, 7.0, 8.2)                  # compartment borders
xm <- (head(xb, -1) + tail(xb, -1)) / 2
num <- c("1  Characteristic\n(position)", "2  Zone shape, value\nand material modifier", "3  Primary\ndatum", "4  Secondary\ndatum", "5  Tertiary\ndatum")
fill <- c("lightcoral", "lightyellow", "lightblue", "lightblue", "lightblue")
ts <- 6 * diagram_text_scale

ggplot() +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = head(xb, -1), xmax = tail(xb, -1), ymin = 0, ymax = 1), fill = fill, color = "black", linewidth = 1) +
  ## position symbol: circle with a cross extending past it
  geom_path(data = circ(xm[1], 0.5, 0.22), aes(x, y), linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = xm[1] - 0.34, xend = xm[1] + 0.34, y = 0.5, yend = 0.5), linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = xm[1], xend = xm[1], y = 0.16, yend = 0.84), linewidth = 0.8) +
  ## tolerance compartment: Ø0.5 followed by a circled M
  annotate("text", x = 2.55, y = 0.5, label = "\u00d80.5", size = ts) +
  geom_path(data = circ(3.75, 0.5, 0.25), aes(x, y), linewidth = 0.8) +
  annotate("text", x = 3.75, y = 0.5, label = "M", size = ts * 0.65) +
  annotate("text", x = xm[3:5], y = 0.5, label = c("A", "B", "C"), size = ts) +
  ## numbered callouts
  geom_segment(aes(x = xm, xend = xm, y = -0.05, yend = -0.35), linewidth = 0.4) +
  annotate("text", x = xm, y = c(-0.65, -0.65, -0.65, -1.15, -0.65), label = num, size = 2.9 * diagram_text_scale, lineheight = 0.9) +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(-0.4, 8.6), ylim = c(-1.45, 1.2)) +
  labs(title = "Feature Control Frame Components") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))
```

### Component Breakdown

| Position | Component | Content | Example |
|----------|-----------|---------|---------|
| 1 | Geometric Characteristic Symbol | Defines the type of control | ⌖ (Position), ⊥ (Perpendicularity), ∥ (Parallelism) |
| 2 | Tolerance Value | Ø if the zone is cylindrical, the total zone width, then any material modifier | Ø0.5 Ⓜ, 0.3 |
| 3 | Datum A | Primary datum reference | A |
| 4 | Datum B | Secondary datum reference | B |
| 5 | Datum C | Tertiary datum reference | C |

### Modifier Symbols

Modifiers are used after the tolerance value and datum references to specify material condition constraints:

- **Ⓜ (Maximum Material Condition)**: the stated tolerance applies when the feature is at MMC; a bonus is added as the feature departs from MMC
- **Ⓛ (Least Material Condition)**: the stated tolerance applies at LMC; a bonus is added as the feature departs from LMC
- **RFS (Regardless of Feature Size)**: the tolerance stays the same at every size. Since ASME Y14.5-1994 RFS is the default when no modifier is shown, so the old Ⓢ symbol is no longer used in ASME drawings
```{r modifiers-table, echo=FALSE}
library(knitr)

modifiers_df <- data.frame(
  Symbol = c("Ø", "Ⓜ", "Ⓛ", "(none)", "Ⓟ"),
  Name = c("Diameter", "Maximum Material Condition", "Least Material Condition", "Regardless of Feature Size (default)", "Projected tolerance zone"),
  Application = c(
    "Cylindrical (circular) tolerance zone",
    "Bonus tolerance as the feature departs from MMC (smallest hole, largest shaft)",
    "Bonus tolerance as the feature departs from LMC (largest hole, smallest shaft)",
    "Same tolerance at every feature size; applies when no modifier is shown",
    "Zone projected above the part, e.g. for holes that receive studs or press-fit pins"
  )
)

kable(modifiers_df, caption=if (knitr::is_latex_output()) "Common GD\\&T Modifiers and Symbols" else "Common GD&T Modifiers and Symbols", booktabs=TRUE)
```

## The Geometric Characteristics

ASME Y14.5-2009 defined 14 geometric characteristics in five categories: form, orientation, location, profile and runout. ASME Y14.5-2018 withdrew concentricity and symmetry (their job is done with position, profile or runout), leaving 12. ISO 1101 still uses all 14, so you will meet both on drawings.

### Form Controls (No Datum Required)

These controls constrain the shape of individual features.
```{r form-controls, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Form Control Characteristics"}
library(ggplot2)

form_controls <- data.frame(
  Symbol = c("⏤", "⏥", "○", "⌭"),
  Name = c("Straightness", "Flatness", "Circularity", "Cylindricity"),
  Definition = c(
    "Line elements (or an axis) lie within two parallel lines (or a cylinder)",
    "The surface lies between two parallel planes",
    "Each circular cross-section lies between two concentric circles",
    "The whole cylindrical surface lies between two coaxial cylinders"
  )
)

kable(form_controls, caption="Form Control Characteristics", booktabs=TRUE)
```

**Example: Straightness**
```{r straightness-demo, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=5.5, fig.align='center', fig.cap="Straightness of a line element, 0.3 mm tolerance, along a 100 mm surface. The zone is two parallel lines 0.3 mm apart (vertical scale greatly exaggerated)."}
## Two measured line elements against a 0.3 mm straightness zone (smooth, deterministic profiles)
x <- seq(0, 100, by = 0.5)
ok  <- 0.08 * sin(2 * pi * x / 55) + 0.035 * sin(2 * pi * x / 14 + 1)      # waviness, peak-to-valley about 0.22
bad <- 0.42 * (x / 100) * (1 - x / 100) * 4 - 0.21 + 0.02 * sin(2 * pi * x / 14)   # bowed, about 0.44
prof <- rbind(data.frame(x, y = ok,  case = "Accepted: peak-to-valley 0.22 mm"),
              data.frame(x, y = bad, case = "Rejected: bowed, peak-to-valley 0.44 mm"))
zone <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(prof, prof$case), function(d) {
  mid <- (max(d$y) + min(d$y)) / 2
  data.frame(case = d$case[1], lo = mid - 0.15, hi = mid + 0.15, pv = max(d$y) - min(d$y))
}))
prof$col <- ifelse(grepl("Accepted", prof$case), "darkgreen", "red")

ggplot() +
  geom_rect(data = zone, aes(xmin = 0, xmax = 100, ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "lightblue", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(data = zone, aes(yintercept = lo), color = "blue", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(data = zone, aes(yintercept = hi), color = "blue", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(data = prof, aes(x, y, color = col), linewidth = 1) +
  scale_color_identity() +
  facet_wrap(~case, ncol = 1) +
  labs(title = "Straightness Control: 0.3 mm Zone",
       subtitle = "Every point of the line element must lie between two parallel lines 0.3 mm apart (dashed)",
       x = "Position along the surface (mm)", y = "Measured deviation (mm)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

### Orientation Controls (Datum Required)

These controls define how features are oriented relative to a datum.
```{r orientation-controls, echo=FALSE}
orientation_controls <- data.frame(
  Symbol = c("⊥", "∥", "∠"),
  Name = c("Perpendicularity", "Parallelism", "Angularity"),
  Definition = c(
    "Feature is perpendicular to datum",
    "Feature is parallel to datum",
    "Feature at specific angle to datum"
  ),
  Use_Case = c(
    "Holes perpendicular to mounting surface",
    "Surfaces parallel for assembly",
    "Angled surfaces at specific degrees"
  )
)

kable(orientation_controls, caption="Orientation Control Characteristics", booktabs=TRUE)
```

### Location Controls (Datum Required)

These controls define where features are positioned.
```{r location-controls, echo=FALSE}
location_controls <- data.frame(
  Symbol = c("⌖", "◎", "⌯"),
  Name = c("Position", "Concentricity (withdrawn in Y14.5-2018)", "Symmetry (withdrawn in Y14.5-2018)"),
  Definition = c(
    "Feature location relative to datums",
    "Feature axis coincident with datum axis",
    "Feature symmetrical about datum plane"
  ),
  Example = c(
    "Bolt hole pattern",
    "Concentric bores",
    "Symmetrical slot"
  )
)

kable(location_controls, caption="Location Control Characteristics", booktabs=TRUE)
```

**Example: Positional Tolerance**
```{r position-demo, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=6, fig.align='center', fig.cap="Positional Tolerance Visualization: the actual hole axis must lie inside a Ø0.7 mm cylinder centred on the true position set by basic dimensions from the datums."}
## Enlarged view around the true position; deviations in mm
rz <- 0.35
cz <- data.frame(x = rz * cos(seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 200)), y = rz * sin(seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 200)))
ax <- data.frame(x = c(0.20, 0.30), y = c(-0.15, 0.22))
ax$d <- sqrt(ax$x^2 + ax$y^2)
ax$lab <- sprintf("%s\n\u0394x = %+.2f, \u0394y = %+.2f\nposition = 2\u00d7%.3f = \u00d8%.2f\n%s",
                  c("Hole 1", "Hole 2"), ax$x, ax$y, ax$d, 2 * ax$d, ifelse(2 * ax$d <= 2 * rz, "ACCEPTED", "REJECTED"))
ax$col <- ifelse(2 * ax$d <= 2 * rz, "darkgreen", "red")

ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = cz, aes(x, y), fill = "lightblue", alpha = 0.5, color = "blue", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "F282", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "F282", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(aes(x = 0, y = 0), shape = 3, size = 4, stroke = 1.2) +
  geom_segment(data = ax, aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = x, yend = y, color = col), linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(data = ax, aes(x, y, color = col), size = 3.5) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.31, y = -0.30, label = ax$lab[1], color = "darkgreen", hjust = 0, size = 3 * diagram_text_scale) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.34, y = 0.33, label = ax$lab[2], color = "red", hjust = 0, size = 3 * diagram_text_scale) +
  annotate("text", x = -0.02, y = 0.03, label = "True position\n(50, 50 basic\nfrom B and C)", hjust = 1, vjust = 0, size = 3 * diagram_text_scale) +
  annotate("text", x = -0.30, y = -0.36, label = "\u00d80.7 tolerance zone", color = "blue", fontface = "bold", size = 3.4 * diagram_text_scale) +
  annotate("label", x = 0, y = 0.47, label = "Position (diameter) = 2 \u221a(\u0394x\u00b2 + \u0394y\u00b2)", fill = "white", linewidth = 0, size = 3.4 * diagram_text_scale) +
  scale_color_identity() +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(-0.5, 0.75), ylim = c(-0.45, 0.5)) +
  labs(title = "Positional Tolerance Example",
       subtitle = "Hole position \u00d80.7 mm at MMC (hole at its MMC size, so no bonus)",
       x = "X deviation from true position (mm)", y = "Y deviation (mm)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

### Profile Controls (Datum Optional)

Profile controls define a uniform boundary around a true profile set by basic dimensions. Without a datum they control form only; with datums they also control orientation, location and size. Profile of a surface is the workhorse control for stampings, castings and plastic parts.

```{r profile-controls, echo=FALSE}
profile_controls <- data.frame(
  Symbol = c("⌒", "⌓"),
  Name = c("Profile of a Line", "Profile of a Surface"),
  Definition = c(
    "Each line element of the feature lies within a 2-D band around the true profile",
    "The whole surface lies within a 3-D band around the true profile"
  ),
  Example = c(
    "Cross-section of an extrusion or airfoil",
    "Stamped bracket, cast housing, plastic cover"
  )
)

kable(profile_controls, caption="Profile Control Characteristics", booktabs=TRUE)
```

## Runout Controls (Datum Required)

These controls define circular or total runout of features about a datum axis.
```{r runout-controls, echo=FALSE}
runout_controls <- data.frame(
  Symbol = c("↗", "⌰"),
  Name = c("Circular Runout", "Total Runout"),
  Definition = c(
    "Each circular element, checked separately while the part turns about the datum axis",
    "The whole surface at once: the indicator is swept along the surface while the part turns"
  ),
  Application = c(
    "Rotating bearing surfaces",
    "Shaft wobble tolerance"
  )
)

kable(runout_controls, caption="Runout Control Characteristics", booktabs=TRUE)
```

## Datum Systems {#sec-datum-systems}

Datums are the foundation of GD&T. They establish the reference framework from which all tolerances are applied.

### Datum Selection Hierarchy {-}

The datum system typically follows a three-plane reference:
```{r datum-system, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=6.2, fig.align='center', fig.cap="Three-Plane Datum System: the part rests on 3 points of the primary plane A, touches 2 points of the secondary plane B and 1 point of the tertiary plane C (3-2-1)."}
## Isometric view; the viewer looks from +x, +y, +z, so the planes x = 0, y = 0, z = 0 are behind/below the part
iso <- function(x, y, z) data.frame(u = (x - y) * cos(pi / 6), v = z - (x + y) * sin(pi / 6))
face <- function(P, id) { d <- iso(P[, 1], P[, 2], P[, 3]); d$id <- id; d }
Lx <- 14; Ly <- 11; Lz <- 8                       # datum planes
bx <- 10; by <- 7;  bz <- 4                        # part block in the corner
planes <- rbind(
  face(rbind(c(0, 0, 0), c(Lx, 0, 0), c(Lx, Ly, 0), c(0, Ly, 0)), "A"),
  face(rbind(c(0, 0, 0), c(Lx, 0, 0), c(Lx, 0, Lz), c(0, 0, Lz)), "B"),
  face(rbind(c(0, 0, 0), c(0, Ly, 0), c(0, Ly, Lz), c(0, 0, Lz)), "C"))
block <- rbind(
  face(rbind(c(0, 0, bz), c(bx, 0, bz), c(bx, by, bz), c(0, by, bz)), "top"),
  face(rbind(c(bx, 0, 0), c(bx, by, 0), c(bx, by, bz), c(bx, 0, bz)), "fx"),
  face(rbind(c(0, by, 0), c(bx, by, 0), c(bx, by, bz), c(0, by, bz)), "fy"))
pts <- rbind(iso(c(2, 8, 5), c(2, 2, 5.5), c(0, 0, 0)),   # 3 points on A
             iso(c(2, 8), c(0, 0), c(2.5, 2.5)),          # 2 points on B
             iso(0, 4, 2))                                # 1 point on C
pts$pl <- c("A", "A", "A", "B", "B", "C")
lbl <- rbind(iso(Lx - 1, Ly - 1, 0), iso(Lx - 1.5, 0, Lz - 1), iso(0, Ly - 1.5, Lz - 1))
cols <- c(A = "lightcoral", B = "lightblue", C = "lightgreen")

ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = planes, aes(u, v, group = id, fill = id), color = "gray30", alpha = 0.75) +
  geom_polygon(data = block, aes(u, v, group = id), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.35, color = "black", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(data = pts, aes(u, v), size = 3.6, shape = 21, color = "black", stroke = 0.8,
             fill = c(A = "red3", B = "blue3", C = "darkgreen")[pts$pl]) +
  annotate("label", x = lbl$u[1], y = lbl$v[1] - 0.6, label = "Primary datum plane A\n3 points (3 DOF removed)",
           fill = "white", color = "red3", linewidth = 0, size = 3.1 * diagram_text_scale, hjust = 0.5) +
  annotate("label", x = lbl$u[2] - 1.2, y = lbl$v[2] + 1.0, label = "Secondary plane B\n2 points (2 DOF)",
           fill = "white", color = "blue3", linewidth = 0, size = 3.1 * diagram_text_scale) +
  annotate("label", x = lbl$u[3] - 0.5, y = lbl$v[3] + 1.0, label = "Tertiary plane C\n1 point (1 DOF)",
           fill = "white", color = "darkgreen", linewidth = 0, size = 3.1 * diagram_text_scale) +
  annotate("text", x = iso(bx / 2, by / 2, bz)$u, y = iso(bx / 2, by / 2, bz)$v, label = "Part", fontface = "bold", size = 4 * diagram_text_scale) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cols, guide = "none") +
  coord_fixed() +
  labs(title = "Three-Plane Datum Reference Frame (3-2-1)") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))
```

### Datum Reference Frame {-}

The Datum Reference Frame (DRF) is a coordinate system established by the datums:
```{r datum-ref-frame, echo=FALSE}
drf_table <- data.frame(
  Position = c("Primary", "Secondary", "Tertiary"),
  Abbreviation = c("A", "B", "C"),
  Contact = c("3 points", "2 points", "1 point"),
  Constraint = c("3 DOF removed (1 translation, 2 rotations)", "2 DOF removed (1 translation, 1 rotation)", "1 DOF removed (last translation)"),
  Feature = c("Main mounting surface (usually the largest)", "Surface perpendicular to A", "Surface perpendicular to A and B"),
  Purpose = c("Sets the first plane and stops rocking", "Aligns the part within plane A", "Fixes the last position; origin at the corner of A, B and C")
)

kable(drf_table, caption="Datum Reference Frame Structure", booktabs=TRUE)
```

## Material Conditions and Bonus Tolerances {#sec-material-conditions}

### Maximum Material Condition (MMC) {-}

MMC is the condition where a feature contains the maximum amount of material:

- Smallest hole diameter
- Largest shaft diameter
- Narrowest slot (and widest tab)
```{r mmc-demo, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Maximum Material Condition Example"}
library(ggplot2)

## Hole diameter tolerances
hole_data <- data.frame(
  condition = c("MMC", "Nominal", "LMC"),
  diameter = c(9.8, 10.0, 10.2),
  description = c("Smallest hole\n(most material)", "Mid-range", "Largest hole\n(least material)")
)

ggplot(hole_data, aes(x=reorder(condition, diameter), y=diameter, fill=condition)) +
  geom_col(width=0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label=diameter), vjust=-0.5, size=5 * diagram_text_scale, fontface="bold") +
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("MMC"="darkgreen", "Nominal"="gray", "LMC"="darkred")) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(9.5, 10.5)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title="Hole Diameter: MMC vs. LMC",
    subtitle="Hole Ø10 ±0.2 mm",
    x="Condition",
    y="Diameter (mm)"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position="none")
```

### Bonus Tolerance {-}

When using MMC modifier, a **bonus tolerance** is granted as the feature departs from MMC. This maximizes functional tolerance while ensuring assembly.
```{r bonus-tolerance, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=5, fig.align='center', fig.cap="Bonus Tolerance Calculation: position Ø0.4 at MMC on a Ø10 ±0.2 hole. The allowed position tolerance grows from 0.4 at MMC (9.8) to 0.8 at LMC (10.2)."}
## Positional tolerance with bonus
actual_size <- seq(9.8, 10.2, by = 0.1)
bonus_df <- data.frame(actual_size = actual_size,
                       positional_tolerance = 0.4 + (actual_size - 9.8))

ggplot(bonus_df, aes(x = actual_size, y = positional_tolerance)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = 0.4, ymax = positional_tolerance), alpha = 0.2, fill = "blue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.4, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.5, color = "blue") +
  geom_point(size = 4, color = "blue") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", positional_tolerance)), vjust = -1, size = 3.5 * diagram_text_scale) +
  annotate("text", x = 9.8, y = 0.36, label = "Stated tolerance 0.4 mm (at MMC)", hjust = 0, size = 3.5 * diagram_text_scale) +
  annotate("text", x = 10.12, y = 0.47, label = "Bonus =\nactual size \u2212 MMC size", size = 3.2 * diagram_text_scale, color = "blue") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Bonus Tolerance Example",
       subtitle = "Position: \u00d80.4 at MMC | Hole size: \u00d810 \u00b10.2 (MMC 9.8, LMC 10.2)",
       x = "Actual hole size (mm)", y = "Allowed position tolerance (mm, diameter)") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(9.75, 10.25), ylim = c(0.3, 0.9))
```

## Common GD&T Applications {#sec-gdt-applications}

### Bolt Hole Pattern {-}

**Problem**: Ensure bolt holes align for assembly.

**Solution**: Use position tolerance relative to three datums.
```{r bolt-pattern, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=6.5, fig.align='center', fig.cap="Bolt Hole Pattern with GD&T: four holes located by basic (boxed) dimensions from datums B and C, with a position tolerance of Ø0.4 at MMC referenced to A, B and C."}
circ <- function(cx, cy, r, n = 100) { a <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = n); data.frame(x = cx + r * cos(a), y = cy + r * sin(a)) }
holes <- expand.grid(x = c(10, 40), y = c(10, 40))
hp <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(holes)), function(i) cbind(circ(holes$x[i], holes$y[i], 3.05), id = i)))
th <- 0.3
arw <- arrow(length = unit(0.14, "cm"), ends = "both", type = "closed")
ts <- 3.3 * diagram_text_scale
basic <- function(x, y, lab, ...) annotate("label", x = x, y = y, label = lab, fill = "white", linewidth = 0.4, size = ts, label.r = unit(0, "pt"), ...)
## feature control frame at (x0, y0): position symbol | Ø0.4 (M) | A | B | C
fx <- 50; fy <- 52; fh <- 4
fb <- fx + c(0, 4, 15, 19, 23, 27)
fm <- (head(fb, -1) + tail(fb, -1)) / 2
## datum feature symbol: filled triangle on the surface, stem, boxed letter
dsym <- function(x, y, dir, letter) {
  if (dir == "down") list(geom_polygon(aes(x = c(x - 1.3, x + 1.3, x), y = c(y, y, y - 1.6)), fill = "black"),
                          geom_segment(aes(x = x, xend = x, y = y - 1.6, yend = y - 4.5), linewidth = 0.4),
                          annotate("label", x = x, y = y - 6.3, label = letter, fill = "white", linewidth = 0.5, size = ts, label.r = unit(0, "pt")))
  else list(geom_polygon(aes(x = c(x, x, x - 1.6), y = c(y - 1.3, y + 1.3, y)), fill = "black"),
            geom_segment(aes(x = x - 1.6, xend = x - 4.5, y = y, yend = y), linewidth = 0.4),
            annotate("label", x = x - 6.3, y = y, label = letter, fill = "white", linewidth = 0.5, size = ts, label.r = unit(0, "pt")))
}
tip <- c(40, 40) + 3.05 * c(cos(pi / 4), sin(pi / 4))

ggplot() +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = 0, xmax = 50, ymin = 0, ymax = 50), fill = "lightsteelblue", color = "black", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_polygon(data = hp, aes(x, y, group = id), fill = "white", color = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
  ## centre lines
  geom_segment(data = holes, aes(x = x - 5, xend = x + 5, y = y, yend = y), linetype = "F282", linewidth = th) +
  geom_segment(data = holes, aes(x = x, xend = x, y = y - 5, yend = y + 5), linetype = "F282", linewidth = th) +
  ## horizontal basic dimensions from datum C (left edge)
  geom_segment(aes(x = c(0, 10, 40), xend = c(0, 10, 40), y = c(-1, 4, 4), yend = -10), linewidth = th) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = 10, y = -8, yend = -8), linewidth = th, arrow = arw) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 10, xend = 40, y = -8, yend = -8), linewidth = th, arrow = arw) +
  basic(5, -8, "10") + basic(25, -8, "30") +
  ## vertical basic dimensions from datum B (bottom edge)
  geom_segment(aes(y = c(0, 10, 40), yend = c(0, 10, 40), x = c(-1, 4, 4), xend = -10), linewidth = th) +
  geom_segment(aes(y = 0, yend = 10, x = -8, xend = -8), linewidth = th, arrow = arw) +
  geom_segment(aes(y = 10, yend = 40, x = -8, xend = -8), linewidth = th, arrow = arw) +
  basic(-8, 5, "10") + basic(-8, 25, "30") +
  ## datum features
  dsym(46, 0, "down", "B") + dsym(0, 46, "left", "C") +
  annotate("text", x = 25, y = 25, label = "Datum A = back face\n(mounting surface)", size = 3 * diagram_text_scale, fontface = "italic") +
  ## hole callout with leader and feature control frame
  geom_segment(aes(x = fx - 2, xend = tip[1], y = fy + fh + 1, yend = tip[2]), linewidth = th, arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.16, "cm"), type = "closed")) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = fx - 2, xend = fx, y = fy + fh + 1, yend = fy + fh + 1), linewidth = th) +
  annotate("text", x = fx + 0.5, y = fy + fh + 1.5, label = "4X \u00d86.0\u20136.2", hjust = 0, vjust = 0, size = ts) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = head(fb, -1), xmax = tail(fb, -1), ymin = fy, ymax = fy + fh), fill = "white", color = "black", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_path(data = circ(fm[1], fy + fh / 2, 1.0), aes(x, y), linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = fm[1] - 1.5, xend = fm[1] + 1.5, y = fy + fh / 2, yend = fy + fh / 2), linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = fm[1], xend = fm[1], y = fy + 0.5, yend = fy + fh - 0.5), linewidth = 0.5) +
  annotate("text", x = fb[2] + 4.2, y = fy + fh / 2, label = "\u00d80.4", size = ts) +
  geom_path(data = circ(fb[3] - 2.2, fy + fh / 2, 1.3), aes(x, y), linewidth = 0.5) +
  annotate("text", x = fb[3] - 2.2, y = fy + fh / 2, label = "M", size = ts * 0.7) +
  annotate("text", x = fm[3:5], y = fy + fh / 2, label = c("A", "B", "C"), size = ts) +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(-18, 80), ylim = c(-14, 64)) +
  labs(title = "Bolt Hole Pattern with Positional Tolerance") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))
```

### Shaft Runout Control {-}

**Problem**: Ensure rotating shaft doesn't wobble excessively.

**Solution**: Apply total runout tolerance about the shaft axis (Datum A).
```{r shaft-runout, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=5.5, fig.align='center', fig.cap="Shaft Runout Control: a section whose axis is offset by e = 0.25 mm from datum axis A makes the dial indicator swing 2e = 0.5 mm per revolution (offset exaggerated)."}
## Cross-section of a shaft turning about datum axis A, with a dial indicator on the surface
circ <- function(cx, cy, r, n = 200) { a <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = n); data.frame(x = cx + r * cos(a), y = cy + r * sin(a)) }
R <- 5; e_draw <- 0.9                       # drawn offset (exaggerated); the real offset is 0.25 mm
rot <- circ(0, 0, R + e_draw)               # path swept by the high point
ggplot() +
  geom_path(data = rot, aes(x, y), linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  geom_polygon(data = circ(e_draw, 0, R), aes(x, y), fill = "lightsteelblue", color = "black", linewidth = 1) +
  ## datum axis A (rotation centre) and feature axis
  geom_point(aes(x = 0, y = 0), shape = 3, size = 5, stroke = 1.2, color = "blue") +
  geom_point(aes(x = e_draw, y = 0), shape = 4, size = 3, stroke = 1, color = "red") +
  annotate("text", x = -0.3, y = -0.9, label = "Datum axis A\n(rotation)", color = "blue", hjust = 1, size = 3 * diagram_text_scale) +
  annotate("text", x = e_draw + 0.3, y = 0.9, label = "Feature axis", color = "red", hjust = 0, size = 3 * diagram_text_scale) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = e_draw, y = -0.3, yend = -0.3), color = "red", linewidth = 0.4) +
  annotate("text", x = e_draw / 2 + 0.6, y = -1.3, label = "e = 0.25 mm", color = "red", size = 3 * diagram_text_scale) +
  ## dial indicator touching the high point
  geom_segment(aes(x = R + e_draw, xend = R + e_draw + 2.2, y = 0, yend = 0), linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = R + e_draw + 2.2, xmax = R + e_draw + 5.2, ymin = -1.5, ymax = 1.5), fill = "gray85", color = "black") +
  annotate("text", x = R + e_draw + 3.7, y = 0, label = "Dial\nindicator", size = 3 * diagram_text_scale) +
  geom_path(aes(x = 7.2 * cos(seq(-0.35, 0.35, length.out = 30)), y = 7.2 * sin(seq(-0.35, 0.35, length.out = 30))),
            color = "darkorange3", arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.12, "cm"), ends = "last")) +
  annotate("text", x = R + e_draw + 3.7, y = -3.2, color = "black", size = 3 * diagram_text_scale,
           label = "Reading swings between\nR + e and R \u2212 e:\nFIM = 2e = 0.5 mm") +
  annotate("text", x = -7, y = -6.2, hjust = 0, size = 3 * diagram_text_scale, color = "gray30",
           label = "Dashed: circle swept by the high point") +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(-7, 12.5), ylim = c(-6.5, 6.5)) +
  labs(title = "Runout: Shaft Turning About Datum Axis A",
       subtitle = "Circular runout 0.5 A: FIM \u2264 0.5 at every cross-section\nTotal runout 0.5 A: FIM \u2264 0.5 with the indicator swept over the whole surface") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5), plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
```

## Tolerance Stack-Up Analysis {#sec-stack-up}

### Worst-Case Analysis {-}
```{r stack-up-worst, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Worst-Case Tolerance Stack-Up"}
library(ggplot2)

## Component dimensions and tolerances
components <- data.frame(
  part = c("Part 1", "Part 2", "Part 3"),
  nominal = c(10, 8, 15),
  lower = c(-0.2, -0.3, -0.25),
  upper = c(0.2, 0.3, 0.25)
)

components$min_size <- components$nominal + components$lower
components$max_size <- components$nominal + components$upper

## Calculate stack-up
nominal_total <- sum(components$nominal)
min_total <- sum(components$min_size)
max_total <- sum(components$max_size)
tolerance_stack <- max_total - min_total

results_df <- data.frame(
  Condition = c("Minimum", "Nominal", "Maximum"),
  Total_Length = c(min_total, nominal_total, max_total)
)

ggplot(results_df, aes(x=reorder(Condition, Total_Length), y=Total_Length, fill=Condition)) +
  geom_col(width=0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label=paste(Total_Length, "mm")), vjust=-0.5, size=5 * diagram_text_scale, fontface="bold") +
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("Minimum"="blue", "Nominal"="gray", "Maximum"="red")) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(32, 35)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title="Tolerance Stack-Up: Worst-Case",
    subtitle=paste("Total Stack-Up Tolerance = ±", tolerance_stack/2, "mm"),
    x="Condition",
    y="Total Length (mm)"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position="none")
```

### Statistical Stack-Up (Optional Advanced Topic) {-}

Statistical stack-up uses probability to reduce required tolerances:
```{r stack-up-statistical, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=5, fig.align='center', fig.cap="Statistical vs. Worst-Case Stack-Up for the three parts above (10 ±0.2, 8 ±0.3, 15 ±0.25 mm), assuming each part tolerance is ±3σ of a centred normal process."}
## Same three parts as the worst-case example
nom <- c(10, 8, 15); tol <- c(0.2, 0.3, 0.25)
wc  <- sum(tol)
rss <- sqrt(sum(tol^2))
sig <- rss / 3                                   # each tolerance taken as 3 sigma
x <- seq(sum(nom) - 1, sum(nom) + 1, by = 0.005)
dd <- data.frame(x, y = dnorm(x, sum(nom), sig))
lims <- data.frame(x = sum(nom) + c(-wc, wc, -rss, rss),
                   method = rep(c("Worst case", "RSS (\u00b13\u03c3)"), each = 2))

ggplot(dd, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_area(fill = "lightblue", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue4", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(data = lims, aes(xintercept = x, color = method), linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = sum(nom) + wc, y = max(dd$y) * 0.9, label = sprintf("worst case\n%.2f", sum(nom) + wc), color = "red", hjust = -0.1, size = 3.2 * diagram_text_scale) +
  annotate("text", x = sum(nom) + rss, y = max(dd$y) * 0.6, label = sprintf("RSS\n%.2f", sum(nom) + rss), color = "blue", hjust = -0.1, size = 3.2 * diagram_text_scale) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Worst case" = "red", "RSS (\u00b13\u03c3)" = "blue"), name = NULL) +
  labs(title = "Tolerance Stack-Up: Statistical vs. Worst Case",
       subtitle = sprintf("Worst case \u00b1%.2f mm; RSS \u00b1%.2f mm contains 99.73 %% of assemblies", wc, rss),
       x = "Total length (mm)", y = "Probability density") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## Practical Exercises {-}

### Exercise 1: Interpreting a Feature Control Frame {-}

**Given**: A part with the following FCF: 
```
┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│ ⌖    │ Ø0.8 │ A │ B │ C │
│      │      │   │   │   │
└─────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Question**: 

- What type of control is being applied?
- What is the tolerance value?
- How many datums are referenced?
- In what order should datums be established?

**Answer**: 
This is a **position control** (⌖) with:

- Tolerance: Ø0.8 mm (circular zone)
- Three datums: A (primary), B (secondary), C (tertiary)
- Datum order of precedence: the order in the frame, A (primary) → B (secondary) → C (tertiary). The part is set on A first (3 points), then pushed against B (2 points), then against C (1 point).

### Exercise 2: Applying GD&T to a Bolt Hole {-}

**Design requirement**: Four bolt holes arranged in a square pattern with hole diameter Ø10 mm on a 40 mm × 40 mm grid. Holes must align within 0.5 mm for assembly.

**Your task**: Create a GD&T specification for this requirement.

**Solution**:
```
- Primary Datum A: Bottom face (mounting surface)
- Secondary Datum B: Left edge
- Tertiary Datum C: Front edge
- Hole size and position: 4X Ø10.0-10.2
                          | ⌖ | Ø0.5 Ⓜ | A | B | C |
- Hole spacing 40 mm as a BASIC (boxed) dimension
  (each axis must lie in a Ø0.5 mm cylinder at its true position;
   more tolerance is allowed as a hole departs from its MMC size, 10.0)
```

### Exercise 3: Tolerance Stack-Up Problem {-}

**Given**:

- Part 1: 10.0 ± 0.1 mm
- Part 2: 8.0 ± 0.15 mm
- Part 3: 6.0 ± 0.1 mm

**Calculate**:

- Minimum total length
- Maximum total length
- Total tolerance stack-up

**Solution**:
```{r exercise3-solution, echo=FALSE}
## Component tolerances
part_1 <- list(nominal = 10.0, tolerance = 0.1)
part_2 <- list(nominal = 8.0, tolerance = 0.15)
part_3 <- list(nominal = 6.0, tolerance = 0.1)

## Calculate stack-up
nominal_total <- part_1$nominal + part_2$nominal + part_3$nominal
total_tolerance <- part_1$tolerance + part_2$tolerance + part_3$tolerance

min_length <- nominal_total - total_tolerance
max_length <- nominal_total + total_tolerance

cat("Minimum total length:", min_length, "mm\n")
cat("Nominal total length:", nominal_total, "mm\n")
cat("Maximum total length:", max_length, "mm\n")
cat("Total tolerance stack-up: ±", total_tolerance, "mm\n")
```

## Try it yourself {#sec-tryit-gdt}

These use features that are not in the examples above. Each exercise checks your answer and lets you try again.

### Bonus tolerance at MMC {#sec-tryit-bonus}

A hole is dimensioned $\varnothing 12.00 \ {}^{+0.10}_{-0.05}$ mm with a position tolerance of $\varnothing 0.25$ mm at MMC. The hole's MMC is its smallest size, $11.95$ mm.

```{r tryit-bonus-grid, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
bn <- data.frame(`Actual hole size (mm)` = c(11.95, 12.00, 12.05, 12.10), check.names = FALSE)
bn[["Bonus tolerance (mm)"]]  <- bn[["Actual hole size (mm)"]] - 11.95
bn[["Total position tolerance (mm)"]] <- 0.25 + bn[["Bonus tolerance (mm)"]]
bn_total_1208 <- 0.25 + (12.08 - 11.95)

tryit_grid(
  id = "bonus-tolerance",
  title = "Position tolerance available at each hole size",
  data = bn,
  blank = c("Bonus tolerance (mm)", "Total position tolerance (mm)"),
  tol = c(`Bonus tolerance (mm)` = 0.005, `Total position tolerance (mm)` = 0.005),
  hints = c(`Bonus tolerance (mm)` = "Bonus = actual hole size - MMC size (11.95 mm). It is zero at MMC.",
            `Total position tolerance (mm)` = "Total = stated position tolerance (0.25) + bonus."),
  digits = 2,
  answers = list(
    tryit_answer("Position tolerance allowed for a hole that measures 12.08 mm", bn_total_1208, tol = 0.005, suffix = "mm",
                 hint = "Bonus = 12.08 - 11.95; add it to 0.25.")
  ),
  intro = "Then decide: would a hole measuring 12.08 mm with a position error of 0.42 mm be accepted?",
  question = paste0(
    "<p>A hole is dimensioned 12.00 +0.10/-0.05 mm, so its limits are 11.95 and 12.10 mm and MMC is 11.95 mm. ",
    "The position tolerance is 0.25 mm diameter at MMC. The bonus tolerance equals the actual size minus the MMC size, ",
    "and the total position tolerance is 0.25 mm plus the bonus. Give the bonus and the total for holes of 11.95, 12.00, 12.05 and 12.10 mm, ",
    "and the total for a hole that measures 12.08 mm.</p>")
)
```

<details class="tryit-solution">
<summary>Show the worked solution</summary>

```{r tryit-bonus-solution, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(bn, digits = c(2, 2, 2), align = "c")
```

At 12.08 mm the allowance is `r sprintf("%.2f", bn_total_1208)` mm, so a measured position error of 0.42 mm is **rejected**. The same error on a 12.10 mm hole (allowance 0.40 mm) would also fail, but 0.38 mm would pass there. The bonus is the whole point of MMC: as the hole gets larger, the position can wander more without compromising assembly.

</details>

### Worst-case against root-sum-square stack-up {#sec-tryit-stack}

Four parts are stacked in a row: $20.00 \pm 0.15$, $12.00 \pm 0.10$, $35.00 \pm 0.20$ and $8.00 \pm 0.05$ mm. The worst-case stack adds the tolerances. The statistical (root-sum-square) stack combines them as $\sqrt{\sum t_i^2}$.

```{r tryit-stack-number, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
st <- list(nom = c(20, 12, 35, 8), tol = c(0.15, 0.10, 0.20, 0.05))
st$nominal <- sum(st$nom)
st$wc      <- sum(st$tol)
st$rss     <- sqrt(sum(st$tol^2))

tryit_number(
  id = "stack-up",
  title = "How much does the stack vary?",
  answers = list(
    tryit_answer("Nominal overall length", st$nominal, tol = 0.01, suffix = "mm", hint = "Add the four nominal sizes."),
    tryit_answer("Worst-case tolerance of the stack (plus or minus)", st$wc, tol = 0.005, suffix = "mm",
                 hint = "Add the four tolerances."),
    tryit_answer("Maximum possible length", st$nominal + st$wc, tol = 0.01, suffix = "mm",
                 hint = "Nominal plus the worst-case tolerance."),
    tryit_answer("Statistical (RSS) tolerance of the stack (plus or minus)", st$rss, tol = 0.005, suffix = "mm",
                 hint = "Square each tolerance, add them, then take the square root.")
  ),
  intro = "Give tolerances to three decimals.",
  question = paste0(
    "<p>Four parts are assembled end to end: 20.00 &plusmn; 0.15, 12.00 &plusmn; 0.10, 35.00 &plusmn; 0.20 and 8.00 &plusmn; 0.05 mm. ",
    "The worst-case stack tolerance is the sum of the tolerances. The statistical root-sum-square (RSS) tolerance is the square root of ",
    "the sum of the squares of the tolerances. Find the nominal length, the worst-case tolerance, the maximum length and the RSS tolerance.</p>")
)
```

<details class="tryit-solution">
<summary>Show the worked solution</summary>

Nominal $= 20 + 12 + 35 + 8 = `r st$nominal`$ mm. Worst case: $0.15 + 0.10 + 0.20 + 0.05 = \pm `r sprintf("%.2f", st$wc)`$ mm, so the length can reach `r sprintf("%.2f", st$nominal + st$wc)` mm.

RSS: $\sqrt{0.15^2 + 0.10^2 + 0.20^2 + 0.05^2} = \pm `r sprintf("%.3f", st$rss)`$ mm, about `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * st$rss / st$wc)`% of the worst case. The statistical figure assumes the parts vary independently and are centred; it allows tighter overall limits, but a few assemblies may fall outside them.

</details>

### Which control category? {#sec-tryit-gdt-categories}

```{r tryit-gdt-sort, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
tryit_sort(
  id = "gdt-categories",
  title = "Form, orientation, location, profile or runout?",
  bins = c("Form", "Orientation", "Location", "Profile", "Runout"),
  cards = data.frame(
    text = c("Flatness", "Cylindricity", "Straightness", "Perpendicularity", "Parallelism", "Angularity",
             "Position", "Concentricity", "Symmetry", "Profile of a surface", "Profile of a line", "Circular runout", "Total runout"),

            "Location", "Location", "Location", "Profile", "Profile", "Runout", "Runout"),

            "Orientation controls refer to a datum.", "Orientation controls refer to a datum.", "Orientation controls refer to a datum.",

  question = "<p>Place each geometric characteristic in its category: form, orientation, location, profile or runout.</p>"

```

### Simulate the stack-up {#sec-tryit-stack-sim}

Worst-case limits add every tolerance. Real parts rarely sit at their limits together. Here four parts are drawn at random (normally distributed, with $\sigma = t/(3 C_p)$) and stacked 20 000 times. The card reports how many assemblies fall outside the worst-case limit and outside the statistical (RSS) limit.

```{r tryit-stack-sim-card, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
qwebr_calc_card(
  label = "stackup-sim-01-04",
  title = "Tolerance Stack-Up Simulator",
  icon = "layer-group",
  inputs = list(
    qwebr_calc_input("seed", "Run number (team number)", value = 1, min = 1, max = 9999, step = 1),
    qwebr_calc_input("Cp", "Process capability C_p of every part", value = 0.8, min = 0.5, max = 2, step = 0.05, type = "slider")
  ),
  rerun = "seed",
  goal = "Raise the process capability until fewer than 0.5% of assemblies fall outside the statistical (RSS) limit.",
  goal_test = "pct_out_rss < 0.5",
  mode = "task")
```

<details class="qwebr-calc-source">
<summary>Show the live R code behind this simulator</summary>
<p>The card above re-runs this exact webR code every time you change an input, substituting your values for the variables at the top.</p>

```{webr-r}
#| label: stackup-sim-01-04
## Four parts stacked end to end, each normally distributed about its nominal
seed <- 1       ## run number: a different number gives a different set of assemblies
Cp   <- 0.8     ## process capability: sigma = tolerance / (3 x Cp)
n    <- 20000   ## number of simulated assemblies

nominal <- c(20, 12, 35, 8)           ## mm
tol     <- c(0.15, 0.10, 0.20, 0.05)  ## mm, plus or minus
sigma   <- tol / (3 * Cp)

set.seed(seed)
total <- rep(0, n)
for (i in seq_along(nominal)) total <- total + rnorm(n, nominal[i], sigma[i])
err <- total - sum(nominal)

wc_tol  <- sum(tol)            ## worst-case tolerance of the stack
rss_tol <- sqrt(sum(tol^2))    ## statistical (root-sum-square) tolerance

pct_out_wc  <- 100 * mean(abs(err) > wc_tol)
pct_out_rss <- 100 * mean(abs(err) > rss_tol)

par(mar = c(5, 5, 3, 1), cex.main = 1.3, cex.lab = 1.2, cex.axis = 1.1)
hist(err, breaks = 60, col = "#aab7c4", border = "white",
     xlab = "Overall length error (mm)", main = "20 000 simulated assemblies")
abline(v = c(-wc_tol, wc_tol), lty = 2, lwd = 2, col = "#c0392b")
abline(v = c(-rss_tol, rss_tol), lty = 2, lwd = 2, col = "#2980b9")

cat(sprintf("Outside the RSS limit of +/-%.3f mm: %.2f%% of assemblies\n", rss_tol, pct_out_rss))
cat(sprintf("  Outside the worst-case limit of +/-%.2f mm   %.2f%%\n", wc_tol, pct_out_wc))
cat(sprintf("  Standard deviation of the stack             %.3f mm\n", sd(err)))
cat(sprintf("  RSS limit expressed in standard deviations  %.2f\n", rss_tol / sd(err)))
```

</details>

## Summary and Key Takeaways {-}

- **GD&T provides unambiguous communication** of engineering design intent
- **Datum systems establish reference frameworks** that organize tolerance zones
- **Bonus tolerance (Ⓜ)**: as a hole grows from its MMC size, its axis may wander further without stopping assembly
- **The geometric characteristics** (12 in ASME Y14.5-2018, 14 in the 2009 edition and ISO 1101) address form, orientation, location, profile and runout
- **Proper application** improves manufacturability, reduces cost, and ensures assembly
